title: kv-prefix-econ-scenarios-q1-2026
summary: Quick scenario spreadsheet exploring combined prefix + KV cache hit-rate permutations and the estimated impact on compute spend. This is an exploratory model (rough unit costs) to surface which hit-rate regimes give the largest marginal ROI for investing engineering time in cache priming and prewarming. Not a finalized pricing recommendation.
calc_assumptions: Assumptions: baseline gen token cost = $1.10 per 1M generated tokens; network/kv lookup overhead = $0.00025 per request; average generation tokens per request = 120; avg prompt (prefix) tokens = 40; percent of prompt tokens served from prefix cache reduces generated tokens proportionally (conservative linear model). We assume 1M requests/month = 30k req/day for scale examples. These are back-of-envelope; validate with runtime billing traces and token logs before committing.

notes: Interpretation of the table: - The "baseline" row is the reference compute-only token bill (gen tokens * unit cost). - "gen_tokens_saved_per_req" = avg_gen_before - avg_gen_after. - We charge a small monthly 'kv lookup overhead' to account for latency/memory overhead; this is intentionally conservative. - High KV hit-rate scenarios reduce backend calls but the engineering cost to reach >80% KV hit for arbitrary workloads is non-trivial (indexing, prompt normalization, TTL tuning). - The largest marginal ROI comes from improving prefix cache hit-rate from modest->high for workloads where prefix tokens are a significant fraction of the request (e.g., long system prompts, repeated instruction templates). - When KV lookups become very frequent (edge_low_latency row), lookup costs and infra pressure exceed simple compute savings; consider batching and local LRU caches on edge tier to avoid remote KV pressure.
recommendations: 1) Pilot: instrument two production routes (chat-assistant and doc-ranker) with prefix cache enabled and collect token-level traces for 2 weeks. 2) A/B: run canary with prefix-only and prefix+KV variants; measure actual token reduction and KV lookup latencies. 3) Metrics: add derived metrics to Console — 'effective gen tokens per req', 'prefix-hit-rate', 'kv-hit-rate', 'kv-requests/sec', 'tokens saved / 1k reqs'. 4) SLO guardrails: cap KV fanout and add circuit-breaker to fall back to model when KV latency spikes. 5) Cost ops: create a dedicated alert for 'KV cost / day' to catch runaway lookup patterns. 6) Product: add a UI toggle in Console for customers to enable prefix caching with suggested TTLs and a cost-savings estimate based on sampled traffic.

open_questions: 1) How do we attribute savings to a customer vs cross-tenant cache effects? 2) Are there sensitive prompts we must avoid caching (PII/PHI) even if they would improve hit-rate? 3) Is the KV store latency deterministic enough for low-latency SLAs or do we need local caching?
